title: Transactional drain protocol to minimize SLO impact during node lifecycle events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Dedicated fleets serve predictable throughput guarantees for customers. Node lifecycle events (OS patches, driver upgrades, reprovisioning) currently rely on best-effort drains that cause transient throughput and latency spikes. Problem: when multiple drains overlap or when KV-cache warmup is slow, customer routes experience degraded p99 latency and throughput SLO violations. Goal: implement a transactional drain protocol that treats a node drain as a coordinated multi-step operation with capacity reservations, KV-cache handoff, and fast rollback to reduce SLO perturbation. The protocol should integrate with autoscaling policies and the existing maintenance window scheduler.
proposal_summary: We will introduce a 4-phase transactional drain: Reserve -> Stage -> Commit -> Verify. Reserve locks a soft throughput reservation on adjacent hosts; Stage transfers KV-cache prefixes and marks draining host read-only; Commit switches routing and drains connections; Verify confirms SLO metrics are within tolerance or triggers automatic rollback. A lightweight coordinator service will orchestrate the phases with idempotent, monotonic state transitions. Exposed controls: one-off drain API, scheduled maintenance mode with phased rollouts, and a conservative default policy that only takes a drain beyond Stage if p99 latency remains below the configured threshold.
design_details:
- Coordinator: small control-plane component per region responsible for orchestration with leader election and persistent state in our existing config-store.
- Reservation: uses tokenized capacity lanes to temporarily reserve 10-20% spare throughput across nodes in the same AZ.
- KV handoff: implement delta-merge transfer of hottest KV prefixes with prioritized lanes so warmup is incremental.
- Routing change: circuit-breaker enabled switch which gradually shifts new requests to healthy hosts while draining does not accept new reservations.
- Telemetry hooks: emit phase entry/exit, reservation utilization, KV transfer bytes, p99/p50/p95 latency deltas, and per-route throughput impact.
- Safety: timeouts and automatic rollbacks if Verify fails or latency degrades beyond threshold for X minutes.
- APIs: POST /fleet/drain/start (with constraints), POST /fleet/drain/commit, POST /fleet/drain/rollback, GET /fleet/drain/status.
- Integration: will plug into autoscaler so scheduled scale-ups consider active reservations and avoid overprovisioning during Stage.
acceptance_criteria: Can perform a transactional drain on a single host without causing p99 > 1.5x baseline for more than 60s
KV handoff completes with <10% cold-cache misses for customer routes within 5 minutes on average
Coordinator survives leader failover and resumes protocol without double-committing drains
APIs return deterministic states and support safe retries (idempotent semantics)
Automated rollback triggers when p99 latency increases >20% sustained for 2 minutes
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Unit/integration tests + canary in staging (week 1)
Stage 2: Dry-run mode in production region with detailed telemetry (week 2)
Stage 3: Enable transactional drains for non-customer-facing maintenance (week 3)
Stage 4: Expand to scheduled maintenance windows and allow tenant opt-in (week 4)
Stage 5: Full default-on for Dedicated fleets after 6 weeks of stable metrics
telemetry_and_alerts: alert: DrainVerifyFailure if p99 delta > 20% for 2 minutes
dashboard: Drain operations per-region with timeline and per-route impact
test_plan: Create synthetic load tests that mimic multi-tenant hot-spot patterns
Simulate leader failover during Stage and confirm rollbacks/continued progress
Chaos run: random node failures + overlapping drain requests
Integration test with autoscaler to ensure reservations are honored
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reservation leads to underutilization and higher cost. Mitigation: conservative defaults with telemetry-led tuning and opt-in policy for existing fleets.
Risk: KV handoff saturates network. Mitigation: rate-limit transfers, prioritize on-ramps during low-traffic windows.
Risk: Coordinator bug double-commits drain. Mitigation: idempotent phase transitions and commit logs with sequence numbers plus canary rollouts.
